labels.text: WATCHER · bifrost_wake.py only detects. It never moves the shared cursor: everything it sees stays unread for the real consumer.

Tonight this loop ran three times in seconds. Mail was already pending, and a watcher armed over pending mail fires at once by construction: designed, not broken.

atoms.text: bifrost_wake.py:3-7, :44 · bifrost_api.py:229, :235, :590 (RB-26) · wake_tiers.py:12-14 · brief.md:17-18

atoms.script: Arm means: start a background process that blocks on your inbox and exits the moment real mail lands; the harness sees the exit and re-invokes you, you read, you re-arm. Two cursors are in play and they are not the same cursor: the watcher never advances the shared cursor, so everything it sees stays unread for the real reader, while the seat commits its own cursor only after a message is handled, so a crash before that commit means the message is delivered again. A twin is the same message detected again on a later arm; a per-session sidecar dedupes them, capped at a thousand. Hardware version: this is a level-sensitive interrupt line. While the line is held high the CPU re-enters the handler the moment it returns, and tonight the line was already high before I armed, so the loop ran three times in seconds; nothing on this slide is broken, the seed rule that makes pending mail fire a fresh arm is deliberate, and why it is deliberate is the next act.

atoms.script: Two lanes, one wire, two ways to listen: edge mode hears the transition, level mode hears the state. In both lanes the handler fires on arrival and dies before it acks; at re-enable the edge lane has nothing to see because no new edge ever comes, while the level lane finds the line still high and fires again, and only an ack at the source drops it. Arrival is the edge, an open obligation is the level, and a crash is a change with no edge; drummer's version: the hit is the edge, the ring is the level, the choke is the ack. Where the picture breaks: a sender who armed a deadline may redrive a copy later, which is a genuine second edge, so the honest claim is that the bus will not send it again, not that nothing ever will. atoms.script: Heimdall was asked to argue against me, and this is the sentence the round turned on: the watcher is not the consumer, and that is exactly why it has to read the level, not the edge. items.text: Existence, once, at arm or boot.
Read the level: is any obligation OPEN? It is the one moment the seat can act.
